note: Low-power transistor technology, Los Gatos; its technology went to Mie Fujitsu Semiconductor in 2015 and the NEA book reads acquired (aligned, rule 10). Incorporated in 2006 with Bill Joy on the board; the 2009 Form D is the first filing on record, not necessarily the entry, and no source read names the round.

Modular cooling and power plants for data centers, Houston (Form D address); the firm lists it acquired by Comfort Systems. A Green Growth Fund position the firm dates to 2011 (the 2013 Form D with John Denniston is a follow-on); no source read names the round.

Free texting and calling app (formerly Gogii), Marina del Rey (Form D address); an iFund position on the firm's 2013-18 pages, the app still operates. The 2015 Form D with Matt Murphy is the only filing on record; no source read names the round the firm entered.

Game studio (Journey, Sky), Los Angeles. The firm dates its investment to 2014, the year of the $7M round led by Capital Today 'and a team of other investors' (Wikipedia), which names no series and does not name Kleiner Perkins; stage undetermined.
Cloud contact center software, San Francisco; still private. The firm's listing gives 2017 and Early; no source read names the round.
Men's apparel brand, headquartered in New York (Wikipedia); private, small Form D rounds in 2024 and 2025.

AI lending platform, San Mateo (Nasdaq: UPST). Wikipedia lists Kleiner Perkins among the investors in the $1.75M seed, the firm's 2012 entry, followed by a named $5.9M Series A, so the seed graduated; the First Round, GV and NEA books also read Seed. Market cap $2.24B on 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis).

Wind turbine operations and maintenance services, Medford, Oregon (the firm's 2010 listing); Vestas bought it (the firm's acquirer field). A Green Growth Fund position entered in 2010 at the $28.8M round with David Mount and Michael Linse as directors; the company was already an operating business, but no source read names the round.
Online marketplace for shipping, Austin (Wikipedia); still private. Aligned with the Benchmark book.

Business payments network (formerly Align Commerce, the firm's page slug), San Francisco (Wikipedia, which lists Kleiner Perkins among the investors). The firm's listing gives 2015 and Early; no source read names the round.
Immunology biotech, Brisbane, California; market cap $2.33B on 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis).

Genomic diagnostics, South San Francisco. The S-1 says the company was incorporated as the incubator Calderome in August 2006 and renamed Veracyte in 2008, with Brook Byers on the board from January 2007, so the firm was a founding investor (its year 2007) and the 2010 Form D date on file is a follow-on; no source read names the first round.

PC power management software, Seattle; Aptean bought it on 2015-01-12 (Wikipedia). The Seed band on the December 2009 Form D is disputed: the firm's own listing carried Verdiem from 2008 and the company dates from 2002, so that filing is a follow-on, and no source read names the entry round.

Domain registry and internet infrastructure, Reston, Virginia (Nasdaq: VRSN). The 1998 IPO registration lists the April 1995 Series A buyers (Bessemer, Visa, Intel, Security Dynamics) without the firm, and Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers VII, its founders fund and the Zaibatsu Fund II buying the February 1996 Series B; Kevin Compton joined the board that month. Market cap $25.47B on 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis).
Columnar analytics database founded in 2005, Billerica, Massachusetts; HP bought it in March 2011 (Wikipedia). The firm's listing gives 2007 with Ray Lane; no source read names the round.

Viant Corp, the Boston internet consultancy (founded 1996 as Silicon Valley Internet Partners; IPO 1999), which merged into divine, inc. in 2002, so acquired, as the TCV book reads, not defunct. The firm's live page mixes in Viant Technology (ticker DSP), a different company. The 1999 S-1 shows KPCB VIII, KPCB Java Fund and related funds holding shares from the 1996 Series A or B, but does not say which.
Access control and compliance software for SAP systems, Fremont; SAP announced the acquisition on 2006-04-03. The firm's listing gives 2004 and Early; no source read names the round.
Diagramming software, Seattle; listed in 1995 and bought by Microsoft in 2000 (Wikipedia, Microsoft Visio). The firm's listing gives 1992 and Early; no source read names the round.

Design-to-code tool for front-end engineers (a Y Combinator company); the firm lists it acquired by Figma and visly.app now redirects to figma.com. No source read places its office or names the firm's 2018 round.

AI stroke and care coordination software, San Francisco. Kleiner Perkins co-led the 2018 $21M Series A with GV (the firm's year 2018, Early). Last priced mark the $1.2B Series D of April 2022, as the GV, Insight and Tiger books record; stale.
Vegetable seed breeding and genetics, South San Francisco (Form D address); Form D rounds through 2020 and no exit found.

Power management semiconductors, Fremont; Maxim acquired it in October 2013. Incorporated in August 1996; the 2004 S-1 shows Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers VIII (a 1996 fund) and related funds as the largest holder and buying Series E, but the first series the firm bought is not named.

Carbon accounting software, San Francisco. $1.8B Series C of February 2024 led by Greenoaks with Kleiner Perkins (company post), stale. The Growth band read off the 2024 Form D is disputed: the firm co-led the 2022 Series B and lists 2020 as its first year, so it entered before, at a round no source read names.

basis: Partner-carried (Erik 2026-09-17 partner-carried rule; D3, D5): the firm's page lists Wave (Toronto) with a 2012 first year, the year of its May 2012 Series B led by The Social+Capital Partnership (Wikipedia), where Mamoon Hamid was a partner; every Form D from 2012 to 2016 names Hamid, who joined Kleiner Perkins in 2017, and no source names a Kleiner Perkins fund in any Wave round. The listing appears only in the 2023-24 logo grid.

note: Autonomous driving, Mountain View. Waymo's own post names Kleiner Perkins among the investors in the $16B round of February 2026 at $126B post-money, the firm's 2026 entry; that round is also the momentum-slice check (done 2026-09-30).

funding_rounds.lead: Dragoneer, DST Global and Sequoia Capital

note: Crowd-sourced navigation, Waze Mobile, most staff in Ra'anana, Israel; Google bought it in June 2013 for about $1.1-1.3B. Kleiner Perkins' Digital Growth Fund entered in 2011, the year of the $30M third round (Wikipedia; the firm co-led it with Horizons Ventures, model knowledge), after the $25M second round of 2010: Growth.

Enterprise application integration software, Fairfax, Virginia; listed in 2000, bought by Software AG in 2007 for $546M (Wikipedia). The firm's listing gives 1996 and Early; no source read names the round.
Automated toothbrush maker; its store still sells (willo.com, 2026-09-30) and the firm lists it Current. No source read places its office or names the firm's 2017 round.

AI coding tools (Codeium, renamed Windsurf), Mountain View. The firm's post says it led the Series B, after the company's Series A. In July 2025 Google licensed the technology and hired the CEO and some staff, which decides nothing (acqui-hire rule); Cognition then signed to buy the company itself (Wikipedia, Cognition AI), so acquired.

basis: Sale consideration (Erik 2026-09-22; decisions.md R5): KPCB China Fund II's Windtree shares (its Form 3 of 2018-12-31) came from Windtree's December 2018 acquisition of CVie Therapeutics, which the fund held (8-K of 2018-12-21, James Huang a former CVie director); Windtree was listed long before, and the 2019 Form D is a private placement into the listed company (T3). CVie Therapeutics is the member.

note: Single-use bioreactor systems, Marlborough, Massachusetts; GE Healthcare bought it in 2012. The firm dates its investment to 2006, so the 2011 Form D (Thomas Monath) is a follow-on and the entry year is the firm's 2006; no source read names the round.

XDx renamed itself CareDx (Nasdaq: CDNA), transplant diagnostics, Brisbane, California (stockanalysis profile); market cap $3.36B on 2026-09-30. Brook Byers' position predates the 2010 Form D on file (listed from 2008); no source read names the round.

Payments infrastructure for Southeast Asia, Jakarta (the Indonesia claim is confirmed, as the Accel, Coatue, Tiger and YC books record). The firm's listing gives 2018 and Early; no source read names its round.
Programmable logic chips, San Jose (Wikipedia); AMD completed the acquisition in 2022. The firm's page says it backed the company in its founding year 1984 but names no round.

basis: Partner-carried (Erik 2026-09-17 partner-carried rule; D3, D5): the live site lists Yammer (Prior, 2010) but no kpcb.com page carried it in any era, even as an alumnus after the 2012 Microsoft sale; the only filing is the 2010 Form D naming Mamoon Hamid, then a partner at US Venture Partners (he joined Kleiner Perkins in 2017), and no source names a Kleiner Perkins fund in any Yammer round.

note: Biopharma, Shanghai (principal office in Pudong; Nasdaq ZLAB). The F-1 shows KPCB China Fund II lending $0.5M on 2014-03-27 as a loan converted into Series A-1 preferred at the August 2014 closing, and buying Series A-1 and A-2; it held 9.3% at the IPO. A KPCB China position (X1).

funding_rounds.round: convertible loan, converted into Series A-1 on 2014-08-20

note: Custom products marketplace, Redwood City (Wikipedia); still private. The firm's listing gives 2004 and Early (Bing Gordon on the archived page); no source read names the round.

Life sciences data and analytics, San Francisco (Form D address). Status aligned with the GV book (acquired). The firm's archived page carries it from 2014, before the 2015 Form D with Brook Byers, so that filing is not the entry; no source read names the round.

Apartment rental marketplace, San Francisco; still private. The firm dates its investment to 2012, before the first Form D (February 2014, Chi-Hua Chien as director), and no source read names the 2012 round.

Social games, San Francisco until the 2022 Take-Two acquisition (then San Mateo). The S-1 records KPCB XIII buying Series B in July 2008 (Bing Gordon's seat), after the January and February 2008 Series A rounds, and the Digital Growth Fund buying Series C in February 2011: Growth.

Fiber network operator, Vancouver (principal office on its 2001 20-F, which Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers signed as an investor party); Kevin Compton was a director from May 2000. Bankrupt in 2001, reorganised in 2002 and bought by Zayo in December 2011 (Wikipedia), so acquired. No source read names the round.
Israeli time-of-flight 3D camera maker (ZCam), Yokneam; sold its assets to Microsoft in 2009, the technology behind Kinect (Wikipedia), so acquired. No source read names the round.
Online diamond retailer, Shanghai, on the firm's 2010 KPCB China portfolio page (X1). No later record of the company was found, so its state is unknown; no source read names the round.

A8 New Media Group, digital music, Shenzhen; listed in Hong Kong in June 2008 and taken private in 2024 by its controlling shareholder's vehicle Lux Origo at HK$0.36 a share (scheme of arrangement, HKEX filings), so acquired. A KPCB China position (X1); no source read names the round.

basis: T3 and X1: AAC Technologies (acoustic components, Shenzhen) has been listed in Hong Kong since 2005 and appears only on the firm's KPCB China portfolio page (2010 on); KPCB China was formed in April 2007, so its position was a purchase in the listed company, or else a pre-2007 TDF-era deal the China listing carried (partner-carried). No Kleiner Perkins private round in AAC is recorded.

note: Apple-harvesting robots, Hayward; shut down in 2021 and its assets were sold, so acquired as the GV book reads (asset sale out of shutdown). On the firm's pages only in 2017-18; no source read names the round.

The firm's page lists 'Accept', 1996, acquired by Amazon: that is Accept.com, the online payments company Amazon bought in 1999. The page's year and its 'enterprise sales productivity software' description do not fit that company and may mix in another; no source read places its office or names the round.
Ultrasound equipment, Mountain View (the firm's 2010 listing); listed in the 1980s (ticker ACN) and bought by Siemens in 2000. No source read names the round.
